newsitem.title: USA: NYS watchdog asks lawmakers to delay casino vote.
newsitem.headline: NYS watchdog asks lawmakers to delay casino vote.

text.p: The New York State comptroller asked lawmakers on Wednesday to postpone a second vote on a constitutional amendment to legalize casino gambling until a federal study on the impact of the industry is finished.

Comptroller H. Carl McCall, who wrote to all the members of the state Senate and the Assembly, said there was a lack of evidence justifying the economic benefits of casino gambling, adding it could hurt citizens who had problems with gambling.

A spokesman for the comptroller had no information immediately available about when the federal commission was expected to finish its job, noting only that five of the nine members had been apppointed and that he expected the panel to work expeditiously.

The state Senate, which is controlled by Republicans, plans to vote on the bill next Monday or Tuesday, according to today's edition of New York Post. The paper said the body wanted to advance its vote to deny the Assembly's Democratic leaders any political leverage over other issues.

The Senate, which is not certain to approve the bill for a second time, initially planned to hold its vote after the Assembly, which is likely to approve the measure. It then could be sent to the voters for a referendum.

McCall, saying that the casino gambling had lost its momentum, added that since 1994, thirty-one states have turned down such proposals and only three have accepted them. He also cited a survey by the Albany Times Union that found New Yorkers opposed legalized casino gambling by a margin of 48 percent to 43 percent.
"I share everyone's concern for the economic well-being of our state, but I've said repeatedly that New York State cannot gamble its way to economic prosperity," McCall said.
